claim.natural: The least n such that every red-blue edge-colouring of K_n contains two vertex-disjoint monochromatic copies of K_4 is 20; the copies need not have the same colour.

limitations: The upper bound reuses this dependency rather than independently reproducing it.
Certificate checks establish unsatisfiability only for the two exact pinned CNFs.
The graph-theoretic reduction, Ramsey-core catalogue, and graph-to-CNF correspondence remain separate, not end-to-end-formalized obligations.
The dependency relation reports only partial semantic alignment and has not been independently audited or externally authenticated.
The z(20) residual cocolourability computations are not dependencies of this claim.
dependencies.statement: For each of the two order-16 (4,4)-Ramsey cores used in the pinned z(20) release, the exact fixed-core CNF over the 64 cross edges is unsatisfiable.

downstream.statement: May be cited only as an unrefereed candidate that VR_2(K_4)=20, where the two disjoint monochromatic K_4 copies may have different colours. The lower bound is a hand-checkable 19-vertex construction with a standard-library verifier; the upper bound reuses the pinned fixed-core UNSAT pair. Exact-CNF certificate checking and a repository-reported one-machine replay do not establish the complete graph-to-CNF equivalence, independent reproduction, complete human review, peer review, or end-to-end formalization. No uniqueness or enumeration of extremal colourings is claimed, and the offline snapshot's lack of objection records is not a complete objection search.

notes: The author-claimed scope is a full exact-value result, but its status is explicitly an unrefereed candidate computer-assisted result. The ClaimPack evidence records are reference-only and mark the release archives as not embedded; the extracted release files supplied in this evaluator bundle were inspected read-only. No applicable adverse assessment was supplied, so DENY is not justified; unresolved positive-policy requirements make UNKNOWN mandatory. This decision is downstream permission under the supplied policy, not a global truth verdict.
